newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP plays down Foster's sale talk.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP plays down Foster's sale talk.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) chief executive officer John Prescott said on Sunday he was not convinced its was a good time for BHP to sell its 37 percent stake in Foster's Brewing Group Ltd.

Asked if it would be a good time to sell the Foster's stake, Prescott repiled: "Well I've heard that expressed, I'm not absolutely convinced of that." He was speaking in a television interview on Channel Nine's Sunday programme.
"I think the full range of possibilities have somehow or other been canvassed with us and we've not made any decisions on any of them," said Prescott in regard to BHP's Foster's stake.

"We've seen Foster's share price improve quite dramatically but it doesn't mean that because we're through a period of restructuring and that we're at the very early stages of growth strategies, that that's a better time than at some other time to make any big decision," Prescott said.
Last month the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported that BHP planned to sell its Foster's stake by the end of its 1996/97 financial year to May 31.
Prescott said BHP would continue to sell mature assets that are no longer relevant to BHP's portfolio of metal, coal, iron ore and steel assets.

"They're not likely to be whole businesses ... but the emphasis is to review each asset one by one and see whether it meets the criteria I've mentioned...Is it low cost? Can it contribute to our growth? Is it having a meaningful impact on a company the size of BHP?," Prescott said.
Last week, Malaysian state-run Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) said it had bought BHP's 43.75 percent stake in Vietnam's Dai Hung oilfield.
